outcome.technical: Worked in <outside-repo> (not committed). drive-phase.py: with executor.writerModel set, the per-task reviewer is now dispatched as `run-agent-session.py --role reviewer` (reviewer_dispatch; model = phase review.model when a full id, else the writer model; prompt file = the Agent dispatch prompt + REVIEWER_SESSION_RULE saying the session files nothing and ends with the return JSON). The drive reads the saved stream (stream_tool_calls counts tool_use blocks in assistant events; unreadable or no assistant message = a stop, never a count of zero), and reviewer_session_step either waits (empty record), or: zero tool calls -> reviewer_unread notes `cannot-tell` on the task once per session and dispatches the reviewer once more (MAX_REVIEWER_REDISPATCH); a second zero-tool session stops with a note naming both sessions and 'no third dispatch', repeated by every later next; a session with tool calls has its last message filed through the existing submit() (return_object extracts the JSON) and the drive goes on as before. Helpers writer_state/open_dispatch/session_record/writer_argv/writer_said/wait_said/note_sessions/session_note gained a defaulted key/role parameter, writer behaviour unchanged; two STEPS + SIGNAL_VERBS rows added (dispatch-reviewer-session, wait-reviewer-session). Why the drive files the reviewer return rather than the session running submit: a session that could run submit makes at least one tool call, so zero tool calls could not distinguish a read from a filing, and a filed return is once-per-start so a re-dispatch after a filed zero-tool return would need a new start. agents/audit-reviewer.md: added 'Open each changed function in the tree before judging.' and cut the same bytes elsewhere (measure-context reviewer entry 6994/7000, GATE OK); tests/test__refs.py ih4 pins 'is not widened by this question', so that sentence was kept (shortened) and the bytes came from '(in the source repository)' -> '(source repo)' and the git-stash sentence. tests: stub claude now emits an assistant event with WS_TOOLS tool_use blocks; new stage rv-block (cases rv1-rv6) and two rows in the sn1 signal corpus. Red-first: first run before any code showed rv1-rv5 FAIL, rv6 PASS (1/6). Mutations on a copy under /tmp: `calls == 0` -> `calls == 99` and `calls < 0` -> rv2 (+rv-block raise) red; `calls <= 3` -> rv5 red (over-fire direction); copy removed. Sweep: tools/sweep-selftests.py 192/194 files; the two reds were tests/test__output_lints.py pn0 (tools/measure-affected-miss.py, the known HEAD red, not mine) and tests/test__refs.py ih4 (mine, fixed; test__refs rerun 292/292). Who-depends: the brief printed no 'Who depends on this' section, so I answered by my own grep: writer_state/open_dispatch/session_record/session_note/note_sessions/wait_said/writer_said/writer_argv have no caller outside drive-phase.py and tests/test_drive_phase.py (sn1 corpus); tools/measure-context.py, tools/lints/_refs.py (red_first_vocabulary_drift, phase_return_key_drift), tools/prove-gates.py and tests/test__refs.py read audit-reviewer.md and all pass. NOT DONE / outside my files: commands/phase.md, reference/orchestrator.md and PLUGIN-BUILD-GUIDE.md still describe the reviewer dispatch only as an Agent; the session path prints a run: line like the writer's. The reviewer body's last paragraph still tells an Agent to run submit; in session mode the prompt overrides it (REVIEWER_SESSION_RULE). Nothing checks that the session opened the RIGHT files, only that it opened some.
outcome.descriptive: Under a writer session setting the per-task reviewer runs as a session whose saved stream the drive reads: a reviewer that opened no file is recorded cannot-tell and re-dispatched once, a second one stops with a note, one that read files is filed and accepted as before.
